To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the design of ECAS for older people can be made easy, fun and effective, using a pipeline that includes free online editors, and BML, and that the use of ECAS can be made more effective, by designing ECAs that match older users’ expectations, in a way that is easy and fun for them.
the online creation and use of 3D embodied conversational agents is feasible, and that older adults can be active participants in the design process.
“The design of embodied conversational agents for older people is feasible, and fun”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of ECAS for older people and their online use.
making ECAs available to older people, and with making older people more involved in designing ECAs for them.
how to build ECAs for older adults, and how they may be used in online settings to address loneliness, social isolation and other social issues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the research on online ECAs and older people is in its infancy.
, in the context of older people, the use of ECAs is not yet a mature field, but there are some promising results.
we are at an exciting stage in the evolution of online embodied agents for older people.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to build online ECAs with the same quality and richness in behaviour as desktop based ones.
we have developed a pipeline for creating online ECAs, and have shown that it is easy for older people to use it.
we have been successful at building an online ECA pipeline, and at designing a first set of female ECAs for older adults.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of ECAS is a very promising approach to address the needs of older people, especially those who live alone.
older adults are able to create and use embodied online ECAs, which are not just for fun but also for learning and social interaction.
the use of ECAs can be a valuable addition to current online services for older people, and that the use of free, open source software and online tools can make this possible, and affordable.
